text.tspan: “Art is how we decorate space,
music is how we decorate time.”
A surface can be faked. A joint cannot: it has
to carry load, and the load path is the one
thing a finish cannot hide. Ask where the load
goes first, then ask what fails getting there.
“Less is only more where
more is no good.”
Subtraction is a measurement, not a style: remove
until the artifact breaks, then put back the last
part you took out. That part is load bearing by
definition, and naming it is the whole entire find.
“Doing things that you express yourself and do
something of the time, is resistance. It’s the
way to go.”
The label is not the work. The work is
what survives its timestamp: a thing is
either of its moment or already dated.
“Anyone can jump a motorcycle;
the trouble begins when you land it.”
A claim is a takeoff. A proof is a landing,
and only one of the two is graded. Staging
a jump is cheap; landing it is not, so the
artifact is what decides it.
“Give the people what they want,
then tell them what they need.”
Build what they asked for, then show them the
failure it hides. Verification comes first
because everything after it is presentation,
and presentation is the cheap half.
“My main objective is to be
professional but to kill him.”
The tool is a hypothesis. The artifact settles
it, and the settling is whatever the diff shows
at the end of the run. A conclusion that cannot
fail is not a conclusion at all; it is posture.
